answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity through stake that is costly to fake: each agent locks collateral that can be slashed on misbehavior, so creating a thousand hollow shells gains nothing because each shell must fund its own stake. Reputation then accrues slowly through attested work, not volume, and newcomers wander through a probationary lane with capped rewards until peers vouch for them — like timber, trust must be grown ring by ring, not conjured overnight.
